XXI Global Open Synchronous Championship


Season 2023–2024



Leg I (17.09 — 02.10.2023)



Notes for the reader:



Please familiarize yourself with the question pack before the game.



Words in caps (e.g., X, FIRST, IT, DO THIS) should be emphasized when reading out loud. After reading the answer, you should also read out other accepted answers and the commentary to the question. Reading out the name(s) of the author(s) is advisable but not necessary. You are also required to tell the players that any open discussion of the game’s questions and results is prohibited until they are disseminated officially.



Certain questions are preceded by additional notes for the reader, in square brackets. You must not read these notes out loud.



Phonetic transcriptions of selected words (in square brackets) are put within the text of some questions for the reader’s convenience.



Handouts for questions 22 and 27 are placed before the text of the questions. Please give the teams some time to familiarize themselves with the handouts, but do not read them out loud.



Good luck!



Round 1


Editors: Alexey Polevoy [paw-lee-VOY] & Denis Rybachuk [ree-bah-CHOOK]


The editors would like to thank the following people: Andrei Kravchenko [KRAFF‑chen‑caw], Peter and Anna Buyny [BOOY‑nee], Timur Yushko, Ruslan Aliev, Timur Sayfullin, Alexander Yermishkin [yerr‑MISH‑kin], Valery Yudachev [yoo‑dah‑CHOFF], Vladimir Muratov, Vladislav Dronov, Alexey Boronenko [boh‑raw‑NEN‑ko], Alexander Pecheny [peh‑CHAW‑nee] and Anton Saksonov.



Question 1.
In New York City, one man always listens to his clients and sometimes asks them to leave their contact details. Using this information, he has started a business of his own, namely a dating agency. Identify him using two words that make up a movie title.

Answer: taxi driver.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: Ahmed Ibrahim, also known as the Cupid Cabbie, matches his passengers together for dates. Driving taxis is a side gig for him, you see, in fact he’s got his own business. The movie Taxi Driver is not romantic at all, but it is set in New York City.

Sources:
1. ‌https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Ibrahim_(Cupid_Cabbie)
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxi_Driver
Author: Denis Rybachuk.

Question 2.
The Museum of the Bible, USA, has a logo that resembles an open book and is made up of THIS turned sideways. Identify THIS.

Answer: the letter В.
Acceptable answer(s): В.
Comment: The logo can be read as an M, for museum, but if one tilts one’s head, it is a B for Bible.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_the_Bible
Author: Alexey Polevoy.

Question 3.
The words DO THIS stand for a multiple‑word phrase. According to a Native American legend, the raven used to be many‑coloured. But then the Earth was engulfed by cold, and the raven had to undertake a long journey to DO THIS. On his way back, he became black. What is the name of the person who DID THIS in another legend?

Answer: Prometheus.
Acceptable answer(s): Matarishvan.
Comment: The raven took the fire from the gods, but while he was carrying it back in his beak, the soot stained him black. Although, if we look closely, the raven’s feathers become rainbow‑hued under sunlight. The Greek hero Prometheus also brought fire to the humans, as did the Indian hero Matarishvan.

Sources:
1. Духовны Д. Мисс Подземка. (David Duchovny, Miss Subways) http://flibusta.is/b/553500/read
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prometheus
3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matarishvan
Author: Alexey Polevoy.

Question 4.
In one short story, preachers say that Native Americans have become dangerous again. The title of the story is THIS. Identify THIS.

Answer: casino.
Acceptable answer(s): Native American casino, Indian casino.
Comment: In 1988, the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act was passed, and Native Americans got the right to build tax‑incentivized casinos in their reservations. The preachers in the story believe that gambling leads people to perdition.

Source: Гришэм Дж. Казино. (John Grisham. Casino) http://loveread.ec/read_book.php?id=73206&p=36
Author: Denis Rybachuk.

Question 5.
A well‑known man tells everyone to be realistic and says, as a joke, that he used to desire Universe, then America, and now he would be satisfied with Brooklyn. What word did we omit from the question three times?

Answer: Miss.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: Taxi driver Ahmed Ibrahim, also known as the Cupid Cabbie, has gradually revised his views about a potential partner.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Ibrahim_(Cupid_Cabbie)
Author: Denis Rybachuk.

Question 6.
In 1796, Étienne‑Gaspard Robert suggested a device which would help France repel a British invasion. The device would be named in honour of a certain person. Identify that person.

Answer: Archimedes.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: Britain was famous for its powerful navy, and to destroy it, the outlandish physicist suggested to use the “mirror of Archimedes”. According to legend, Archimedes focussed reflected light on the Roman fleet which was besieging Syracuse and burned it down. However, Robert got short shrift and later tried to implement his ideas elsewhere.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Étienne-Gaspard_Robert
Author: Rodion Polevoy.

Question 7.
In the novel The Gates of Athens, a character is warned that his detractors are breaking Xes. The X cut became popular again thanks to The Beatles. Identify X using only one word.

Answer: bowl.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: The character gets a warning that his enemies want to exile — or ostracize — him. For the voting, shards of pots and bowls, called ostraca, would be used. The bowl cut is very old, but it became popular again thanks to The Beatles’ early look.

Sources:
1. Иггульден К. Врата Афин. (Conn Iggulden, The Gates of Athens) http://loveread.ec/read_book.php?id=108798&p=51
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowl_cut
Author: Denis Rybachuk.

Question 8.
The protagonist of a novelty song is despairing and decides to use paints. The object that is featured in this song was created in 1974. By whom?

Answer: Ernő Rubik.
Acceptable answer(s): the surname Rubik is sufficient.
Comment: The character wants to save the humanity from going insane while trying to solve the puzzle. Painting it in the right colours is easier than completing it correctly.

Sources:
1. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XKewhUMDqJY
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernő_Rubik
Author: Alexey Polevoy.

Question 9.
In the late 19th century, numerous art objects were looted from a certain country. In the early 2000s, campaigners for restitution of this looted art noted serious issues in communication with the current owners. Identify the country.

Answer: Nigeria.
Acceptable answer(s): Republic of Nigeria, Federal Republic of Nigeria.
Comment: The campaigners sent many letters to museums and private collectors, not to gain any profit, but in a genuine effort to bring back the bronzes looted by the British in 1897. But the letters stayed unanswered. This might have been due to the so‑called “Nigerian letters”, whose authors spammed email messages with outlandish stories to lure people into sending them money.

Source: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/w3ct4xjs
Author: Alexey Polevoy, who has spent years writing questions to raise money for a ticket to Nigeria, where his millions have been waiting for him in a bank vault.

Question 10.
In 1963, the Bristol X Company, founded in the previous century, refused to employ a black person. This led to a boycott of the company. The word X itself might have played a role, as it implies equality. Identify X.

Answer: Omnibus.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: Like in Montgomery, US, where Rosa Parks refused to rise from her seat, activists boycotted the city bus company. The word omnibus means “for all” in Latin.

Sources:
1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_Omnibus_Company
2. https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/w3ct4xb1
Author: Alexey Polevoy.

Question 11.
In this question, the two BLANKs stand for an identical multi‑word phrase. As a reason not to employ Guy Bailey, the Bristol Omnibus Company cited the concern that Bailey would not be BLANK. What do traffic rules advise pedestrians to do in order to be BLANK?

Answer: wear high visibility clothing.
Acceptable answer(s): answers with the same general sense, using words “high visibility clothing/vest”, “hi vis/viz”, “yellow vest”, “fluorescent”, “retroreflective” and other synonyms.
Comment: The BLANK stands for “visible in the dark”. The Bristol Company cited several absurd reasons for not employing Bailey, and even identified the time when he would become invisible as 7 pm.

Source: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/w3ct4xb1
Author: Alexey Polevoy.

Question 12.
One of the Bristol anti‑racism campaigners later recalled that he realized just how successful their actions were, only when he heard eager congratulations from a Bristol…
‌Who?

Answer: taxi driver.
Acceptable answer(s): cabbie, taxicab driver.
Comment: The boycott was supported by many locals. A cabbie recognized the campaigner and told him he was now getting more passengers than ever. The boycott was successful and became one of the factors leading to the introduction of anti‑racism laws in the UK.

Source: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/w3ct4xb1
Author: Alexey Polevoy.

Round 2


Editor: Ruslan Aliev

Question 13.
Shortly before the coup in Egypt, Anwar Sadat went to a cinema together with his wife, and there he had a scuffle with another spectator. One author writes that Sadat did this to get THIS. Identify THIS using only one word.

Answer: alibi.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: Should the coup fail, and Sadat become a suspect, he would be able to point out that at the time of the coup he had been in the cinema and then in the police station. However, the coup succeeded, and Sadat became one of the country’s rulers.

Source: Юджин Роган. «Арабы. История. XVI–XXI вв» (Eugene Rogan, The Arabs: A History); https://flibusta.is/b/564593/read
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 14.
In the 19th century, some Egyptian officers were sent to serve in the South. A historian writes that for Egypt, THIS was an equivalent to THAT. Identify THIS and THAT, using words beginning with the same letter.

Answer: Sudan, Siberia.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: Eugene Rogan writes that for Egyptians, being exiled to Sudan was akin to Siberian exile in the Russian Empire. Both regions had climates that the exiled were not used to: while Siberia had cold, Sudan had heat even more intense than in Egypt.

Source: Юджин Роган. «Арабы. История. XVI–XXI вв» (Eugene Rogan, The Arabs: A History); https://flibusta.is/b/564593/read
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 15.
In a certain novel, the female main character is gassed by Nazis and is about to die of asphyxiation. She is however saved by a resistance fighter. She copes with the traumatic memory, and later she tells her granddaughters her own version of a well‑known story. Identify the title of this story using only two words.

Answer: Sleeping Beauty.
Acceptable answer(s): Briar Rose.
Comment: In the novel, the Nazis throw the bodies of the prisoners they kill into a pit, but the resistance fighters hiding nearby notice that one Jewish girl is still breathing. One fighter gives her the “kiss of life”, and she survives to then travel to the USA and live a long life. She never mentions her traumatic experience directly, only through the story of the Sleeping Beauty, who was revived by a prince’s kiss.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Briar_Rose_(novel)
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 16.
The left hand is often associated with femininity, the right one with masculinity. In a late 20th‑century work of fiction, SHE is shown as left‑handed, which creates additional difficulties for her. Identify HER name.

Answer: Mulan.
Acceptable answer(s): Hua Mulan.
Comment: The Disney heroine who joined the Chinese army had to pass off as not just a male, but a right‑handed male, because soldiers were trained to wield their swords right‑handed. This created additional difficulties, but she overcame them. In Chinese philosophy, the female principle is associated with the left‑hand side, and the male principle with the right‑hand side, and in the movie, Mulan uses her left hand when she displays femininity.

Sources:
1. https://www.libraryanswer.com/is-left-side-yin-or-yang/
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yin_and_yang
3. https://twitter.com/joppashmat/status/1690747014324068353
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 17.
The mencey, indigenous chieftains of a certain island, saw themselves as radically different from the rest of their people, and eventually this led to a specific set of problems. Ironically, in the 16th and 17th centuries their island was under the rule of THEM. Identify THEM using a proper name.

Answer: Habsburgs.
Acceptable answer(s): the Habsburg dynasty/family, the house of Habsburg.
Comment: The mencey were chieftains among the Guanche, the indigenous people of the island of Tenerife. They married only top members of nobility, to emphasize that they were distinct from ordinary people. On a sparsely populated island, this led to inbreeding and extinction of the dynasty. The Canary Isles were captured by Spain in the 15th century, which was later ruled by the Habsburg dynasty. The Habsburgs suffered from inbreeding even more, as king Charles II had multiple genetic disorders and was infertile, which led to the extinction of their Spanish line.

Sources:
1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guanches#Political_system
2. https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mencey
3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenerife
4. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Habsburg
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 18.
If you download a certain version of the game Quantum Break, you will be able to see the main character wearing THIS. A Spanish noblewoman who can be seen with THIS on a portrait, was nevertheless famous for her beauty. Identify THIS using one or more words.

Answer: eyepatch.
Acceptable answer(s): eye patch.
Comment: The developers made a joke about those who download pirated games. There are no limitations to the gameplay, but the main character wears a pirate‑style eyepatch. Spanish noble lady, Princess of Eboli, was one‑eyed, but still became famous for her beauty and even became the prototype for the main heroine in the play Don Carlos and its opera adaptation.

Sources:
1. https://za.ign.com/quantum-break/99498/news/quantum-break-pirate-detection-gives-players-eye-patches
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ana_de_Mendoza_y_de_Silva,_Princess_of_Éboli
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 19.
USA’s first female astronaut Sally Ride recalled that journalists asked mostly dumb questions. For example, whether she was going to DO THIS in zero‑G. What phrase does DOING THIS stand for?

Answer: wear a bra.
Acceptable answer(s): accept answers that mean the same.
Comment: Instead of stressing Sally’s gruelling training regimen and her heroism, journalists asked stereotyped questions. For example, they suggested that in zero‑G she would not need a bra.

Source: Рэйчел Свейби. «52 упрямые женщины. Ученые, которые изменили мир» (Rachel Swaby, Headstrong: 52 Women Who Changed Science — and the World); https://flibusta.is/b/693802/read
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 20.
Art historian Dmitri Sarabyanov compared THEM to Luddites. Among THEM was the famous son of a Carbonaro, who fled abroad from persecution. Identify THEM using only one word.

Answer: Pre‑Raphaelites.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: Just like the Luddites called for a stop to industrial innovations and urged the world to get back to manual labour, the Pre‑Raphaelites dreamed of returning to the immediacy and simplicity of early Italian art before Raphael. One of their most famous members, Dante Gabriel Rossetti, got his name in honour of Dante Alighieri, whom his father revered. The elder Rossetti was also a founder of the Carbonari secret society.

Sources:
1. Анна Познанская, Инесса Ципоркина. «Прерафаэлиты. Революция в викторианском искусстве»; https://flibusta.is/b/739764/read
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriele_Rossetti
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 21.
A character in an American TV series, who is forced to spend some time in a karaoke, mentions THIS. One argument for giving THIS back is that the treaty was unequal. Identify THIS.

Answer: Guantanamo.
Acceptable answer(s): Guantanamo Bay, Guantanamo detention camp, Guantanamo Bay Naval Base, other similar designations.
Comment: The character is forced to listen to his brother singing and makes a joke about Guantanamo, the detention camp infamous for inmates being tortured with loud music. The area where the camp stands has been under permanent lease from Cuba since early 20th century. Since Fidel Castro came to power, Cuba has asked for the territory to be given back, because, as a smaller country, it was forced by the USA to enter the lease treaty. So far they have not been successful.

Sources:
1. Succession. S04, E02, ~42:46
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guantanamo_Bay_Naval_Base
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 22.
[Handout:
Beyond *********
]
In early 21th century, a certain corporation tried to improve its public image by investing in solar power, and used the slogan you see on the handout. Identify the word hidden by the asterisks.

Answer: Petroleum.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: British Petroleum, an oil and gas company, tried to pose as a champion of the environment and used the slogan Beyond Petroleum, which can also be abbreviated as BP. But despite its efforts in renewable energy, its public image could not recover from the 2010 oil rig explosion and oil spill in the Bay of Mexico.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BP
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 23.
Double 2 questions with 30 seconds’ conferring for each, the answers must be handed in on a single slip.
It is apparent that the second question of the two is much worse than the first one.
1. In an alt‑history narrative, one country succeeds in reforming itself and reconquers the Middle East. In this narrative, the country is nicknamed THIS. Identify THIS using exactly five words.
2. The individual who is mentioned as the first THAT once saw locals make something like muskets out of palm leaves. Identify THAT using exactly three words.

Answer: 1. The healthy man of Europe.
2. Smoker of Europe.
Acceptable answer(s):
1. The strong/healed/recovered man of Europe.
2. Smoker in Europe.
Comment: In this alt‑history narrative, the Central Powers won the First World War, and the Ottoman Empire underwent reforms under the Young Turks and recaptured lost ground in the Middle East. In the 19th century it was called “the sick man of Europe” for its failure to adapt and constant loss of territory, but in this imaginary version the empire is the healthy man. Sailor Rodrigo de Jerez, who travelled with Columbus, saw the natives make impromptu cigarettes out of palm leaves and fill them with tobacco. The burning cigarette looked like a musket to the Spaniards. Later, Rodrigo himself became a tobacco smoker. If you felt like the first question was a healthy man’s question and the second one was a smoker’s question, like they say in the popular meme, then you were right. That was the point.

Sources:
1. https://youtu.be/4Mu0FDtt4V4?t=16
2. https://youtu.be/4Mu0FDtt4V4?t=106
3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_de_Jerez
4. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_tobacco
5. https://bb.lv/statja/vazhnaja-data/2022/10/12/kak-zhestoko-byl-nakazan-za-svoyu-strast-pervyy-kurilshchik-evropy
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Question 24.
From the 1650s, Rembrandt’s paintings became dominated by dull earthy colours. According to one interpretation, this is due to the painter’s THIS. Identify THIS using a word that ultimately comes from Italian.

Answer: bankruptcy.
Acceptable answer(s): only the exact answer is accepted.
Comment: The painter struggled to make ends meet and had to save on paints. Earthy colours were cheaper than things like ochre and vermillion, so his paintings took a brownish hue. The English word “bankrupt” is made of Latinized roots but traces its origin from the Italian phrase banca rotta — broken bench.

Source: Пол Симпсон. «Код цвета» (Paul Simpson, The Colour Code); https://flibusta.is/b/704428/read
Author: Ruslan Aliev

Round 3


Editor: Anvar Muhametkaliev [moo-ha-MET-kah-LEE-yeff]


The editor would like to thank: Idelia Ayzyatulova [eye‑za‑TOOL‑oh‑vuh], Ruslan Aliev, Nikolai Archak, Valery Yesaulov [yay‑sah‑OO‑loff], Alexander Korobeynikov [core‑oh‑BEY‑nick‑off], Darya Mashtak, Maxim Merzlyakov [mers‑lya‑KOFF], Eugene Mirotin [mee‑RAW‑tin], Daniil Pakhomov, Alexander Pecheny [peh‑CHAW‑nee], Yuri Razumov, Anton Saksonov, Alexander Taranik, Ulyana Fabrichnina [ool‑YAH‑nuh fah‑BRITCH‑nee‑nuh], Nail Farukshin [nah‑EEL far‑ROOK‑shin].



Question 25.
Due to narrow streets and overpopulation, wheeled vehicles were banned within the city of Ancient Rome. Tom Standage writes that Caesar allowed wheeled vehicles to move around… Complete this sentence using a film title from the mid‑1990s.

Answer: From Dusk till Dawn
Acceptable answer(s): translations of the title.
Comment: For a long time, Rome had had to make do with mules and human porters. To speed up trade and construction, Caesar allowed the use of vehicles at times when they would not bother the populace.

Sources:
1. T. Standage. A Brief History of Motion: From the Wheel, to the Car, to What Comes Next.
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/From_Dusk_till_Dawn
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 26.
In the early 1980s one of the founders of the band Chumbawamba blindfolded himself, sat down and started doing a certain thing. Allan Wallie tells this story and mentions… which animals?

Answer: monkeys.
Acceptable answer(s): apes, chimps, chimpanzees.
Comment: According to the famous saying, if a hypothetical monkey is pressing the keys of a typewriter for an unlimited length of time, it will end up typing any given text. The band members wanted a unique name for the band, and so one of them sat at a typewriter blindfolded and started typing. Out of the collection of nonsense words that he typed, the band liked the word chumbawamba.

Sources:
1. A. Dolgins. The Big Book of Rock & Roll Names: How Arcade Fire, Led Zeppelin, Nirvana, Vampire Weekend, and 532 Other Bands Got Their Names.
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinite_monkey_theorem
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 27.
[Handout:
Artists in Residence
]
The Artists in Residence gallery, intended for female artists, was initially to be named after a work of fiction from mid‑19th century. In one film adaptation of this work, the main character was played by an actress named Charlotte. Identify this work.

Answer: Jane Eyre.
Acceptable answer(s): Jane Air.
Comment: Artist Howardena Pindell suggested the name Eyre Gallery, after Charlotte Bronte’s character. But in the end, they chose a similar‑sounding acronym A.I.R., which stands for Artists in Residence. In one adaptation of Charlotte Bronte’s novel, Jane was played by Charlotte Gainsbourg.

Sources:
1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.I.R._Gallery
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howardena_Pindell
3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Eyre_(1996_film)
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 28.
It is told that in 1929 one avid enthusiast waited for a special moment and then brought a close family member THERE. Then the story mentions a rare name, Airleen. What does THERE stand for?

Answer: on board of a plane.
Acceptable answer(s): answers with the same meaning, using words like “airplane”, “aircraft”, “flight” etc.
Comment: Airleen is likely to be the first child born in an aircraft. That is why her name begins with Air. The avid fan of flying brought his wife, who was soon due, into a plane and they stayed in the air until the baby was delivered.

Source: https://www.cntraveler.com/story/what-happens-to-babies-born-on-planes
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 29.
Writer Stanislava Przybyszewska [stan‑ee‑SLAH‑vah pshee‑bee‑SHEF‑ska] was preoccupied with the French Revolutionary era. Alexis Angulo recalls that in her personal letters she often used THESE. Which one of THESE became the title of an 1885 novel?

Answer: germinal.
Comment: Przybyszewska was obsessed with Maximilien Robespierre and even made him the main character in her most famous book, the play Danton’s Case. In her later years she was poor and isolated and communicated mainly through letters. In these letters she often used the months of the French Revolutionary calendar. Germinal is a classic novel by Emile Zola.

Sources:
1. https://culture.pl/en/article/stanislawa-przybyszewska-a-brilliant-playwright-preoccupied-with-revolution
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germinal_(novel)
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 30.
Charles Darwin wrongly believed that the females of practically all species have one specific thing in common. Lucy Cooke compared this view to a certain object. Stories about the use of such objects in the Middle Ages became popular in Darwin’s times. Identify this object using only two words.

Answer: chastity belt.
Comment: Darwin’s views of reproduction were decidedly Victorian. In fact, monogamy and passivity are not common to all females. Chastity belts are unlikely to have existed in the Middle Ages, and they are only mentioned jokingly in various books from the period. Most of the purportedly medieval devices shown in museums are 19th‑century forgeries.

Sources:
1. L. Cooke. Bitch: On the Female of the Species.
2. https://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/everything-youve-heard-about-chastity-belts-is-a-lie
3. https://medium.com/@editors_91459/turns-out-chastity-belts-were-just-fake-news-from-the-middle-ages-a1eb3cc3434
4. https://www.encyclopedia.com/social-sciences/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/chastity-belt
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 31.
In a certain work of fiction, a family tradition is shown. After a certain event the children board a ferry. When it has covered some distance, they throw THIS into the water. Identify THIS.

Answer: tooth.
Acceptable answer(s): milk tooth, also in plural.
Comment: In many countries, when a child loses a milk tooth, it is symbolically given to the tooth fairy. This family tradition is built on the fairy—ferry pun.

Sources:
1. Only Murders in the Building, S03E05.
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_fairy
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 32.
Martin Heidegger’s thought was not limited by existing boundaries. A biographer quotes a common English phrase and adds that for Heidegger there was no such thing as a… Complete the sentence using a short English word.

Answer: box.
Comment: According to his biographer, Heidegger did not just think outside the box, he came to the conclusion that there is no box.

Source: В. Айленбергер. Время магов. Великое десятилетие философии. 1919‑1929. (Wolfram Eilenberger, Zeit der Zauberer. Das große Jahrzehnt der Philosophie 1919 — 1929)
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 33.
The city of Hull in England was often visited by merchants from lands to the east. According to one interpretation, THESE on Hull’s coat of arms are a reference to a well‑known story. Another instance of THESE became the nickname of… which national team?

Answer: Sweden [national ice hockey team].
Acceptable answer(s): Swedish.
Comment: THESE stands for “three crowns”. It is believed that the three crowns on the coat of arms symbolize the Three Kings who came from the East. Three crowns are also a symbol of Sweden. The Swedish national hockey team got the nickname Tre kronor — three crowns — in 1938, when they wore jerseys with this design at the World Championship.

Sources:
1. https://www.hullhistorycentre.org.uk/research/research-guides/three-crowns.aspx
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden_men's_national_ice_hockey_team
3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Crowns
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 34.
Rod McKuen spent the early 1950s in a certain Asian country. He claimed to have invented THIS to make the “northerners” go back to their girlfriends. Write THIS.

Answer: Make love not war.
Acceptable answer(s): any translation of the motto.
Comment: During the Korean War, McKuen was responsible for radio propaganda, and later he claimed to have coined the famous anti‑war motto. However, he was known to be mendacious, and his authorship has not been proven.

Sources:
1. https://slate.com/culture/2022/10/rod-mckuen-best-selling-poet-songs-what-happened.html
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Make_love,_not_war
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 35.
Rod McKuen tried to keep up with the popular trends. In the early 1960s, he released a dance song with the title featuring HIM. In one screen adaptation, HE was a stray kitten. Identify HIS name and surname.

Answer: Oliver Twist.
Comment: It is believed that the twist craze of that time was due to the success of Chubby Checker’s version of The Twist. McCuen jumped on the bandwagon with his own song titled Oliver Twist. Dickens’s character Oliver Twist was an orphan boy. The adaptation mentioned is Disney’s Oliver & Company.

Sources:
1. https://slate.com/culture/2022/10/rod-mckuen-best-selling-poet-songs-what-happened.html
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_&_Company
3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twist_(song)
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev

Question 36.
It is believed that THEIR modern use was popularized by William Wirt. He used THEM to streamline the way his charges would go between a limited number of rooms. Another theory states that THEY were implemented to get people used to factory hours as early as possible. Identify THEM using two words.

Answer: school bells.
Comment: In the town of Gary, schoolchildren were divided into groups. At the sound of a bell, each group went to the room assigned to their next class. John Taylor Gatto, a former teacher, believed that school undermined human spirit and curiosity, and bells were invented to train working‑class children to follow a factorylike schedule.

Sources:
1. https://hackeducation.com/2022/01/30/bell
2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Taylor_Gatto
3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Wirt_(educator)
Author: Anvar Muhametkaliev
